task_specification.objective: Repair the ordinary player-facing release path first—authored cemetery spatial integrity, five-wave terminal/retry lifecycle, and upgrade-choice presentation—then harden the opt-in dense-profile handoff so native hardware recapture can qualify representative final-wave performance without changing ordinary gameplay or replacing preserved authored assets.

diagnosis.root_cause: The ordinary release path is not closure-ready because the cracked bell's hard-coded collision footprint is misaligned with its rendered instance, blocking trustworthy five-wave traversal and retry evidence. The dense profile correctly rejects llvmpipe, but native 1920x1080 qualification remains unavailable; candidate work should preserve a recapture-ready native handoff rather than fabricate a pass. The upgrade presenter must remain an authored visual hierarchy with truthful values and complete input focus states.

stop_conditions: Produce exactly two bounded tasks whose gap_ids cover each required gap exactly once.
Keep the intact authored cemetery package, Warden Lantern, Gravespade, and Wandering Wisps identities; do not split, replace, or surgically edit preserved source assets.
Do not claim native dense-performance qualification on the current llvmpipe/software renderer; retain rejected software evidence and stop after candidate-side handoff readiness.
Keep tester/runtime recapture, visual review, and formal issue closure in validation rather than implementation tasks.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause treatment for the repeatedly treated ordinary route issue: restore one authoritative authored-instance binding and derive landmark collision/perimeter data from the rendered footprint, while keeping route progression and terminal ownership authoritative. Treat dense performance as a renderer-gated qualification handoff, adding only missing candidate-side receipt integrity and never emulating native results.

code: Run Godot parse/import checks on all touched GDScript and scene files.

Run the dense profile side-effect-free self-audit and focused route/upgrade transaction assertions, including duplicate terminal, held-confirm, malformed-offer, renderer-gate, and reset-isolation cases.
Verify release-export guards remove all tester/validation InputMap actions and that no private or debug presentation paths are introduced.
runtime: Tester recaptures ordinary title -> gameplay -> five contiguous waves -> Bellkeeper -> Result using ordinary input, then exercises failure and at least three isolated Retry/Title cycles; bind WaveDirector, RunController, collision transforms, build selection, result statistics, and replay receipts to the exact candidate.

Tester replays spawn, central building/landmark, cracked bell, perimeter/boundary, and ordinary movement/movement replay cells with the same camera framing, checking collision alignment, escape lanes, external depth, disappearance, and occlusion.

Tester opens the real upgrade draft at native and reduced UI scales with keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, verifies visual hierarchy, choice hierarchy, silhouettes/icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, selected build state, and observable post-choice combat change.

Tester runs tester_dense_prepare -> tester_dense_advance -> tester_dense_reset serially for three cycles on native hardware at 1920x1080 and 25-40 enemies; on llvmpipe, retain rejected software status and inspect the handoff rather than issuing a qualification verdict.
visual: Compare shipped high-angle cemetery composition against the bound Mournlight reference: readable lantern post, mausoleum, cracked bell, escape lanes, moonlit blue-violet shadows, warm lantern lighting, and no visible proxy or placeholder geometry.

Inspect the full upgrade page at native, fullscreen/windowed, and supported UI scales for visual hierarchy, choice hierarchy, icon-first silhouettes, compact aligned current-to-new deltas, restrained transparent surfaces, and distinct focus/hover/pressed/unavailable states without clipping or overlap.

Inspect dense final-wave frames only after the runtime receipt confirms representative enemy, weapon, pickup, HUD, animation, VFX, lights, and audio coverage; reject any visual claim based solely on telemetry.

done_when: The cracked bell collision is derived or rebound from the rendered bell footprint in the same world-space instance, with no substantial vertical overhang or mismatch; player and enemy movement replay can pass on every side while preserving a traversable route.

The authored cemetery is presented at a larger traversable scale that visibly expands into a coherent external world/external depth band; the central building and every landmark remain stable, readable, and grounded from spawn, route, cardinal, and close traversal views.

All gameplay collision, route anchors, spawn lanes, and the perimeter/boundary agree with visible geometry; ordinary movement cannot produce pass-through, disappearance, or camera occlusion drift at the landmark or boundary.

The ordinary five-wave route advances contiguously through all five authored wave ids and Bellkeeper, commits exactly one victory or failure Result, and performs isolated Retry and Title resets without stale actors, pause ownership, timers, audio, input latches, or duplicate terminal transitions.

The upgrade draft uses a clear choice hierarchy and authored visual hierarchy: each option leads with weapon or upgrade silhouettes/icons, compact stat icons, and truthful current-to-new values with no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas; CURRENT never uses NEW or LOCKED placeholders, unchanged or exhaustive rows are omitted, and copy stays restrained.

Keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states, hover states, pressed states, and unavailable states are visibly distinct without changing card dimensions; the selected id, rank, and applied modifier match authoritative build state and the next combat event visibly reflects the choice.

Tester can use ordinary successful runs (not diagnostic fixtures) to distinguish focused bolts, close-range sweeps, and orbiting area-control build shapes and to reach the release result statistics, credits/provenance, and replay surfaces.
tasks.instructions: Repair the ordinary release surface across the authored world binding, route director/controller handoff, and real upgrade-draft presenter. Rebind the cracked bell collision from the instantiated rendered AABB or an equivalent authoritative footprint calculation instead of repeating isolated transform nudges; keep the cemetery as one intact authored package with additive collision/navigation/spawn data only. Ensure contiguous ordinary wave progression—not tester jumps—gates Bellkeeper eligibility and exactly-once Result, Retry, and Title cleanup. Inspect and adjust the actual draft scene/controller only where needed to provide a clear choice hierarchy and visual hierarchy: silhouettes/icons first, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, restrained copy, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states. Preserve truthful catalog projections and debounced selection. Do not add proxy roads, duplicate landmarks, replacement map assets, or debug-only UI. This task must explicitly expand the larger traversable scale, preserve external world/external depth, keep the central building/landmark collision aligned, prevent disappearance/occlusion, maintain boundary/perimeter integrity, and prove ordinary movement/movement replay.

done_when: The dense contract remains editor-only and release-disabled, with stable contract signature, target viewport 1920x1080, target density 25-40 (32 target), and bounded prepare -> advance -> reset protocol.

When frames execute, advance receipts retain nonzero frame and physics sample counts plus frame/physics/render distributions, occupancy/churn metrics, subsystem coverage, lifecycle deltas, and runtime-error counts even before renderer qualification is applied.

Renderer classification is explicit: native hardware may qualify only with hardware_qualification_eligible=true; llvmpipe/software remains rejected_software_renderer with sampling diagnostics retained, never converted to a pass.

Three serial dense cycles preserve cycle_id/cycle_index, run_serial, setup_generation, advance_generation, requested/resolved workload, and reset_next_frame isolation with zero live actors and active ordinary input context; duplicate, timeout, stale, and delayed controls are bounded and rejected.
The dense profile does not alter ordinary wave pacing, weapon behavior, HUD presentation, or release exports, and the host handoff receipt names the exact native recapture prerequisites for Tester.
tasks.instructions: Audit the existing DenseWaveProfile and RunController collector boundary and make only minimal candidate-side repairs needed for a native recapture-ready handoff. Preserve the renderer gate after sampling: collect real frame/physics metrics whenever frames run, surface nonzero sample availability and bounded high-churn/lifecycle counters, then classify hardware/software/unknown explicitly. Preserve editor-only tester_dense_prepare/advance/reset actions, idempotency, cycle identity, reset isolation, and the three-cycle aggregation contract; never synthesize frame-time data or treat llvmpipe as native. If the current detector and handoff already satisfy these predicates, leave gameplay code unchanged and limit edits to missing receipt fields or self-audit assertions.
